messages.subject: Binary Indicator for Competition Covariate
parts:
To my fellow occupancy analysts, 

I'm trying to aproximate the co-occurrence of two species using MacKenzie's 2-species model, and am interested in assessing to what extent (if any) the species are in competition with one another. A simple solution to this, I would assume, would be to include a binary covariate indicating sites where both species were present and then assessing whether or not the model containing this covariate is the best model. My concern, is that there is a limited number (roughly 20%) of sites where the species do co-occur. Therefore, my expectation is that this covariate will falsely describe much more of the variance than it normally would assuming there were more sites where the species co-occurred. Any helpful suggestions on how I might get around this problem? 

Thanks,

Josh

messages.author: 7ac258fb6a0ab492
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Binary Indicator for Competition Covariate
parts:
Dear Josh,
It is my understanding that the 2-species models of MacKenzie (2004), Richmond (2010), and others are not yet implemented in 'unmarked', but I am sure someone will correct me if I'm wrong or if that is in the works.

If both species are detected imperfectly, it will be difficult to create a covariate that *perfectly* measures co-occurrence. However, building encounter histories for each species and modeling detection explicitly may offer some alternatives. See a useful discussion here for more thoughts. 

I've used the Richmond parameterization (which is more stable for use with covariates) in MARK (it's also available in PRESENCE), and you can derive a species interaction factor (SIF; described in Richmond 2010) that may provide the inference you're interested in.

Best,
Brittany
